images.filename: Early Morning on Scafell Pike. - geograph.org.uk - 496238.jpg
images.caption:
Early Morning on Scafell Pike. I had climbed the Pike the previous evening with the intention of photographing the sunset and then the sunrise.  Low cloud prevented me from doing either.
I had been kept awake by shouts of triumph and squeals of delight from national three peak challengers right up until 10pm.  The following morning my first visitors came within earshot as I was taking these pictures - at 4.30!
images.alt:
Early Morning on Scafell Pike. I had climbed the Pike the previous evening with the intention of photographing the sunset and then the sunrise.  Low cloud prevented me from doing either.
I had been kept awake by shouts of triumph and squeals of delight from national three peak challengers right up until 10pm.  The following morning my first visitors came within earshot as I was taking these pictures - at 4.30!

images.caption: Cairns and Marked Slabs Anyone who has climbed Sca Fell Pike via the Corridor route will recognise these slabs on the NW side of the mountain.  No doubt, the criss-cross pattern is natural, but I couldn't offer any reason how they came to be there.
images.alt: Cairns and Marked Slabs Anyone who has climbed Sca Fell Pike via the Corridor route will recognise these slabs on the NW side of the mountain.  No doubt, the criss-cross pattern is natural, but I couldn't offer any reason how they came to be there.

images.caption: Crossing the col Lingmell Col in a snow shower.  The ascent of Scafell Pike, England's highest hill is relatively quiet via Lingmell.  The final stretch to the summit would see us passing several walkers, poorly equipped for the conditions.  A fact of life on a must-bag summit.
images.alt: Crossing the col Lingmell Col in a snow shower.  The ascent of Scafell Pike, England's highest hill is relatively quiet via Lingmell.  The final stretch to the summit would see us passing several walkers, poorly equipped for the conditions.  A fact of life on a must-bag summit.

images.caption: Col Between Broad Crag and Scafell Pike Walkers ascending Scafell Pike via The Corridor Route from Styhead have a choice. A route to Lingmell Col off to the right or this ascent up the screes of the upper reaches of Piers Gill. I know which I would choose.

images.caption: Foxes Tarn View looking towards Scafell Pike on a day of very good visibility.  At a time when the Lords Rake route was not recommended due to the dangers of possible rock fall, the route via Foxes Tarn made for a logical alternative to a walk between Scafell and Scafell Pike.  The main drawback of this route is that the descent involved has to be regained in approaching Mickledore.
